sections.title: What is a Trie?
sections.content:
A Trie (prefix tree) is a tree where each path from root to a node spells out a prefix of some stored string. Every node has up to 26 children (for lowercase English) plus a boolean `isEndOfWord` marking whether a complete word ends there.

The power of a trie over a hash set is **prefix queries**. A hash set answers 'does apple exist' in O(1) but cannot answer 'does any stored word start with app' without scanning everything. A trie answers that in O(L) — walk down 3 nodes and check whether you landed on a valid node.

This makes tries the go-to for autocomplete, spell checkers, IP routing, and any problem where a **dictionary of words** must be queried by prefix. Word search on grids benefits from tries: instead of a separate DFS per word, build a trie from the dictionary and run one DFS that prunes branches the moment no trie path matches.

Memory is the main trade-off. Each node holds up to 26 child references. But for prefix-heavy workloads tries win on both query speed and conceptual clarity.

In interviews tries appear explicitly ('implement autocomplete') or implicitly as an optimization for brute-force word search.

sections.title: When to Use This
sections.content: Use a Trie when the problem involves a dictionary of words and you need to query by prefix — not just exact match. If 'words starting with', 'autocomplete', 'longest common prefix', or 'search with wildcards' appears, a Trie is the direct tool.

sections.title: Trie Node Structure and Operations
sections.content:
## Node Structure

`children`: Map from char → TrieNode. `isEndOfWord`: boolean, true if a complete word ends here. The character is encoded on the **edge** (key in parent's children map), not inside the node.

## Insert — O(L)

Walk each character, create nodes as needed, set `isEndOfWord = true` after last character.

## Search (Exact) — O(L)

Walk characters; return false if any is missing. At end, return `node.isEndOfWord`. The flag is essential — without it, searching 'app' returns true even if only 'apple' is stored.

## StartsWith (Prefix) — O(L)

Same walk; return true if you successfully traverse all prefix characters without hitting a missing node. No `isEndOfWord` check.

## Trie + DFS (Word Search II)

Build a Trie from the word list. DFS on each board cell; at each step check if the current character exists as a child in the current Trie node. If not, **prune immediately**. When `isEndOfWord` is reached, record the word. Dramatically faster than per-word DFS.

## Deletion

Lazy: set `isEndOfWord = false`. Proper: recursively delete nodes with no children and `isEndOfWord = false` after removing the word.

items.name: Trie with Wildcard Search
items.description: When '.' matches any character, branch into all children at wildcard positions via recursive DFS over the trie. TrieNode structure is unchanged.

items.name: Trie + DFS for Board Word Search
items.description: Build Trie from word list. DFS on each board cell tracking the current Trie node. Prune if next character has no matching child. Record words when isEndOfWord is reached. Far faster than per-word DFS.

items.name: Compressed Trie (Patricia Trie)
items.description: Merge chains of single-child nodes into one node storing a substring. Reduces space for sparse tries where long paths have no branching. Rarely implemented from scratch in interviews.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.time: O(L) per insert/search/startsWith where L is string length
sections.space: O(N × L) where N is number of words and L is average length
sections.explanation: Each operation walks at most L nodes doing O(1) Map lookup at each. Space is O(N × L) worst case when words share no prefixes. Shared prefixes reduce actual node count. Using a 26-element array instead of Map gives O(1) indexing at the cost of O(26) space per node regardless of branching.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Forgetting isEndOfWord makes it impossible to distinguish 'app' (stored) from 'app' as a prefix of 'apple' — search('app') incorrectly returns true when only 'apple' is inserted.
Using node.children[c] with a plain object without hasOwnProperty check can cause false positives on inherited properties like 'constructor'. Use Map or check explicitly.
Not handling case sensitivity — trie nodes are typically built for lowercase a-z. Mixed-case input without normalization leads to silent misses.
In Word Search II, not removing found words from the Trie after discovery causes duplicate results when the same word is reachable via multiple board paths.
Confusing which node stores a character — the character 'a' is on the edge from root to root.children['a'], not stored inside the child node itself.

items.title: Word Search II
items.why: Trie + DFS combination — tests the pruning optimization where the Trie drives DFS and eliminates dead-end paths early.

items.title: Longest Word in Dictionary
items.why: Incremental Trie construction — a word is only valid if every prefix of it is also in the Trie, requiring isEndOfWord checks at each step.

sections.title: What to Learn Next
sections.why: BFS and DFS are the foundational Level 5 graph algorithms. Tries already introduce tree traversal for string paths; BFS/DFS generalize that to arbitrary graphs. Word Search II is literally Trie + DFS on a grid — graph traversal is already in your toolkit.
